text: Preface The occupational and environmental safety and health professions have been on merging paths for several years now.

Preface
The occupational and environmental safety and health professions have been on merging paths for several
years now.

text: Corporate "down-sizing" or "right-sizing" has resulted in a more streamlined approach to these once very diverse and quite separate disciplines.

Corporate "down-sizing" or "right-sizing" has resulted in a more streamlined approach to these
once very diverse and quite separate disciplines.

text: Although they both may now be practiced in tandem, often by the same individuals, each has evolved and developed as a separate area of study.

often by the same individuals, each has evolved and developed as a separate area of study.

text: ©2000 CRC Press LLC E ear A structure within and external to the side of the head consisting of three major aspects (external ear, middle ear, and inner ear), which is used for hearing and equilibrium.

E
ear
A structure within and external to the side of
the head consisting of three major aspects
(external ear, middle ear, and inner ear),
which is used for hearing and equilibrium.

text: The outer ear consists of the auricle, or pinna, and the external acoustic meatus.
text_raw:
The outer ear consists of the auricle, or pinna,
and the external acoustic meatus.

text: The auricle collects sound waves and directs them to the external acoustic meatus which conducts them to the tympanum (the cavity of the middle ear).
text_raw:
The auricle
collects sound waves and directs them to the
external acoustic meatus which conducts them
to the tympanum (the cavity of the middle
ear).

text: The tympanic membrane (eardrum) separates the outer ear from the middle ear.
text_raw:
The tympanic membrane (eardrum)
separates the outer ear from the middle ear.

text: In the middle ear are the three ossicles: the malleus (referred to as the "hammer" because of its shape), the incus (or "anvil") and the stapes (or "stirrup").
text_raw:
In the middle ear are the three ossicles: the
malleus (referred to as the "hammer" because
of its shape), the incus (or "anvil") and the
stapes (or "stirrup").

text: These three small bones form a chain across the middle ear from the tympanum to the oval window in the mem- brane separating the middle ear from the inner ear.
text_raw:
These three small bones
form a chain across the middle ear from the
tympanum to the oval window in the mem-
brane separating the middle ear from the inner
ear.

text: The middle ear is connected to the naso- pharynx by the Eustachian tube, through which the air pressure on the inner side of the eardrum is equalized with the air pressure on its outside surface.
text_raw:
The middle ear is connected to the naso-
pharynx by the Eustachian tube, through
which the air pressure on the inner side of the
eardrum is equalized with the air pressure on
its outside surface.

text: The middle ear is also connected with the cells in the mastoid bone just behind the outer ear.

The middle ear is also
connected with the cells in the mastoid bone
just behind the outer ear.

text: Two muscles at- tached to the ossicles contract when loud noises strike the tympanic membrane, limiting its vibration and thus protecting it and the in- ner ear from damage.

Two muscles at-
tached to the ossicles contract when loud

text: In the inner ear (or labyrinth) is the cochlea, containing the nerves that transmit sound to the brain.

In the inner ear (or
labyrinth) is the cochlea, containing the
nerves that transmit sound to the brain.

text: The inner ear also contains the semicircular canals, which are essential to the sense of balance.

inner ear also contains the semicircular canals,

panic membrane to vibrate.

text: The ossicles function as levers, amplifying the motion of the tympanic membrane, and passing the vi- brations on to the cochlea.

in any other Place." The first immunity is of

conduct impulses.
